articles.title: Penny Lane Is Dead review – Aussie slasher comedy zips from Neighbours to nasty
articles.summary: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status. Here is a muddled if energetic effort from Australian writer-director Mia’Kate Russell.
body: Set in Australia in 1986 (presumably because this means no mobile phones, and thus no calling for help), a trio of high-school besties prepares for a night of partying before the summer ends. Penny (Bailey Spalding) is planning to go to university to study law and asks her girlfriend Toni (Tahlee Fereday) to come with her. The two have only recently become lovers and they haven’t yet come out to their buddy Amy (Alexandra Jensen) – a sweet, childlike teen who still carries a stuffed tiger toy around for comfort.

And they most certainly haven’t come out to Kat (Sophia Wright-Mendelsohn, daughter of Aussie actor Ben Mendelsohn) – an erstwhile friend with whom they haven’t hung out for a while and who they didn’t think would show up that evening. Except here she is, bearing cupcakes for each of them with insults piped on the top in icing. Kat, it turns out, has drugged Penny’s cake, so she passes out and Kat’s super-skeevy ex-con boyfriend Angus (Ben O’Toole) shows up with his leather-clad crew – and suddenly it all goes from an episode of Neighbours to The Last House on the Left.
points: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status.
Here is a muddled if energetic effort from Australian writer-director Mia’Kate Russell.

articles.title: Oscars: Belgium Picks Lukas Dhont’s Cannes Prizewinning ‘Coward’ for International Feature Race
articles.summary: Lukas Dhont’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the international feature film race at the 99th Academy Awards. The selection marks the third time Belgium has submitted a film by Dhont to the Oscars.
body: Lukas Dhont ’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the international feature film race at the 99th Academy Awards.
The movie was lauded at Cannes where it was bought by Mubi for a number of major territories, including the U.S., U.K., Spain, Italy and Latin America.

“I am truly honored that we get to represent Belgium at the Oscars this year with ‘Coward.’ We look forward to sharing our film with the world and with Belgian audiences,” said Dhont, who has become one of Belgium’s most internationally acclaimed filmmakers.”‘Coward’ celebrates togetherness in broken times, connection in a fragmented world. We hope that ‘Coward,’ which above all celebrates the power of the heart, will offer a moment of tenderness and comfort,” Dhont added.
Dhont once again collaborated on “Coward” with several members of his longtime creative team, including co-writer Angelo Tijssens and cinematographer Frank Van den Eeden, among others.

articles.title: George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and More Set for Finch & Partners and CAA’s ‘Future of Creativity’ Forum in Venice
articles.summary: Presented by Finch & Partners and CAA, the invitation-only forum is titled “The Future of… Creativity” and, according to a press release, aims to gather “leading
body: George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and more are set to take part in an inaugural forum themed around creativity in Venice next month, held alongside the film festival.

The forum builds on the inaugural “Future of… Film” event held during the Cannes Film Festival in May, which featured Darren Aronofsky, James Gray, Nadine Labaki, Whit Stillman and J.A. Bayona as well as executives from Mubi, A24, Sony Pictures Classics, Neon, Focus Features and Sony Pictures. The Venice edition is set to “broaden the conversation beyond film to examine how AI and other technological changes are transforming creativity across disciplines and what that means for the future of culture itself,” according to the release.

Co-head of CAA Media Finance Roeg Sutherland said that the forums “convene those who shape culture and are dedicated to sustaining and protecting art — in all its forms, while embracing new forms of expression and innovation that celebrates the human experience.”

articles.title: Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo After Paramount Calls His Merger Attack ‘Antisemitic’: ‘Those of Us With a Platform Need to Use Our Voices’
articles.summary: “Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder has come to the defense of Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused him of invoking “antisemitic tropes” when criticizing the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.
body: On her Instagram Story on Monday night, Einbinder — who is Jewish and has been an outspoken advocate for Palestinians — became the first major celebrity to publicly support Ruffalo. “I’m so grateful that Mark Ruffalo drew a connection between the Ellisons providing military technology to Israel during a genocide and their unprecedented media takeover — and pointed out that this is a dangerous consolidation of power that could ultimately be used against us,” she wrote.

“The idea that he only said these things because the Ellisons are Jewish is LUDICROUS,” Einbinder continued. “Is it also antisemitic to point out that Safra Catz, the Oracle executive vice chair who boasted about the ‘profoundly scary technology’ provided to the IDF, also sits on Paramount’s board? Or that Larry Ellison has been buying favor with Trump by donating tens of millions to his political effort for years? Or that he once offered Netanyahu a lucrative Oracle post?”

articles.title: Zip Wire review – cancer-curing scientist is on the hook for cable-dangle thriller
articles.summary: This nonsensical film sees an OCD-afflicted scientist fending off assassins while hanging from an aerial wire, and fails to get pulses racing for even a minute. In this silly, low-adrenaline thriller, the title star is a rickety old zip wire bolted into the side of a mountain in the Italian…
body: The scientist is Amy (MyAnna Buring); she has discovered a cure for lung cancer, and her drive is explained in syrupy hospital-ward flashbacks to her mother dying when she was a teenager. Amy also has OCD – she is so anxious about germs that she never takes off her rubber gloves, and has an assistant in her lab to do anything that involves touching or handling objects. (Like all the characters, she never gets beyond a stereotype.) Her research is bankrolled by a big pharma company, whose CEO is played by Saffron Burrows (now seemingly mandatory casting for ropey British thrillers).

Amy’s gamechanging discoveries result in an old-school conspiracy, involving a notebook with her research written in code and a trio of contract killers. Which is how Amy ends up in the Dolomites (where everyone has an English accent), halfway across a zip line. Supposedly, a human body cannot remain in a state of maximum panic for more than 30 minutes, but Amy seems to bat away her terrible fear of heights in about five minutes flat. For the audience, you’ll be lucky if this gets your pulse racing for more than two of them.

articles.title: Crooked Media Is Bringing Back Nate Silver’s ‘FiveThirtyEight Politics’ Podcast, Which Will Relaunch Next Month as ‘Still Counting’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: FiveThirtyEight is coming back from the dead — sort of. Just ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Crooked Media inked a deal to acquire and revive the “FiveThirtyEight Politics” podcast hosted by Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke.
body: Now Silver, Malone and Druke are back in the saddle with Crooked Media, the progressive media company best known for “Pod Save America,” hosted by former Obama administration staffers Jon Favreau, Jon Lovett, Tommy Vietor and Dan Pfeiffer. Crooked said the “Still Counting” hosts will bring “a no bullshit, clear-eyed approach to the wonky ins and outs of politics without losing the humor and personality that make the conversation fun.”

Silver, in the trailer for “Still Counting” ( watch below ), says: “There’s a ton of data and information coming at us every day, and a surprising amount is misunderstood or under-explained. Numbers are hard, takes are easy. We’re taking a step back to ask: What does the data actually say, and how can we use it to better understand the future of American politics?”

The podcast will explore three key questions, according to Silver: what does the data actually say?; how do we reconcile that with the other things that we’re seeing in American politics and around the world?; and “how do we use that to understand or maybe even dare to predict the future of American politics?”

articles.title: ‘Environmental violence’: inside the fight to save indigenous land from becoming a nuclear dumping ground
articles.summary: New documentary To Use a Mountain spotlights the pain and triumph of resisting government efforts to turn parts of rural US into disposal sites. Nuclear energy was supposed to be our salvation, humanity’s chance to retool technology first conceived as a weapon of mass destruction into an engine of…
body: To Use a Mountain could exist as a coda to Christopher Nolan ’s Oppenheimer, showing how the Manhattan Project physicist’s fears about nuclear technology’s vast potential for devastation proved more justified than even he could have imagined. In particular, the film trains its lens on the passage of the 1982 Nuclear Waste Policy Act – which, among other things, placed six rural communities across the US in a derby of sorts to become the permanent site for more than 90,000 tons of high-level nuclear waste.

Not surprisingly, the Department of Energy disposal list quickly homed in on sparsely populated rural communities that mining and farming industries had left behind. In some cases, those communities were largely made up of marginalized Black and brown people whose claims to the land date back generations. Advocates against the Yucca Mountain site argue that its designation as a DoE nuclear disposal ground disregards a US government treaty obligation to the Western Shoshone tribe. The area’s history of seismic activity is another reason to be wary of Yucca’s structural integrity over the ensuing millennia.

articles.title: Kate Hudson to make How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days sequel, 23 years on
articles.summary: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.
body: A sequel to How to Lose a Guy In 10 Days is in development, more than 20 years after the original hit rom-com was released, with original star Kate Hudson set to produce.
Work on the film is in the "very early days", with sources telling US media, external that both Hudson, 47, and Matthew McConaughey, 56, could reprise their roles from the first film.

In the original, Hudson played a magazine journalist called Andie who researches an article about modern dating. She convinces her boss she can get a man, Benjamin (McConaughey), to leave her in 10 days. Meanwhile, Benjamin bets his boss he can make any woman fall for him, with Andie his target.
Hudson will produce the sequel alongside Stacey Sher, who is behind hits such as Pulp Fiction and Matilda.
points: Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, her co-star from the 2003 rom-com, could be reunited for the sequel.

articles.title: Russian stadium says it won't host Kanye West gigs
articles.summary: Two planned concerts are thrown into doubt, but Russian promoters insist they will go ahead.
body: The Russian stadium that was scheduled to host two shows by Ye, the rapper also known as Kanye West, has said the events will no longer take place.
In a social media post, external, St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said no rental agreement had been signed with the concert promoters. "Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site."

West would have been the first major Western performer to play Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The rapper is trying to rehabilitate his image after years of antisemitic remarks, for which he recently apologised.
Gazprom Arena acknowledged it had received complaints about West's planned appearance and stressed that it "was not and is not" responsible for his booking.

articles.title: Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo From Paramount “Antisemitism” Claim: “All of Us Artists Could Stand to Be More Like Mark”
articles.summary: The Emmy-winning 'Hacks' actress added that Ruffalo was "fighting for the working class of Hollywood" in his opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger deal.
body: Hannah Einbinder has come out strongly in defense of Mark Ruffalo as the actor faces an accusation of “antisemitism” from Paramount Skydance over his opposition to the studio’s deal for Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD).

Over the weekend, Ruffalo fired back at Paramount, saying that the studio accusing him of antisemitism is “appalling and fundamentally dishonest.” “Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people,” Ruffalo said in a viral X post that has now been viewed by 30 million users, retweeted over 163,000 times and liked over 861,000 times.
